capitals.name: Valletta
capitals.note: 'The country's capital is Valletta'; the State of Malta page also gives Valletta.

correction.text: the islands of Malta, Gozo and Comino as the independent State of Malta from 21 September 1964

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Malta row begins in 1967 but 'Malta gained independence as the State of Malta on 21 September 1964'; the seed lists no earlier Cliopatria row for the islands, so the 1967 outline is carried back three years.

474.7 km2 against the infobox 316 km2 (no year on the page): ratio 1.50, within a factor of two; the grid rounds a three-island state up to whole cells. The page records no change in the islands after 1964: the British lands given up in 1979 lay inside the outline. Only Malta, Gozo and Comino are named as inhabited.
Same outline and area (474.7 km2) as 1967-2023.

region.text: the islands of Malta, Gozo and Comino

ledger.note: 1964: Malta becomes independent as the State of Malta on 21 September. 'Malta gained independence as the State of Malta on 21 September 1964'; 'Under its 1964 constitution, Malta initially retained Elizabeth II as Queen of Malta' with a governor-general (the State of Malta page: 'existed between 21 September 1964 and 13 December 1974', Sir Maurice Dorman governor-general, Giorgio Borg Olivier first prime minister).

1974: Malta becomes a republic on 13 December. 'Malta declaring itself a republic on 13 December 1974 within the Commonwealth'; the State of Malta page: the monarchy was abolished and a president appointed by Parliament. The land is unchanged.

region.text: 'lands formerly controlled by the British were given to the Maltese government'

ledger.note: 1979: the British leave on 31 March. 'A defence agreement was signed soon after, and after being re-negotiated in 1972, expired on 31 March 1979', 'the British base closed and lands formerly controlled by the British were given to the Maltese government'. The base lands lie inside the existing outline, so no cell changes hands; the page gives no area or place names, hence region = the whole state and confidence 2.

certainty.note: An island group: the coastline is the frontier. The page records no territorial or maritime dispute with Italy or Libya (sea limits are not land).

sources.title: Malta

sources.title: State of Malta
sources.note: 1964-1974 dominion: dates 21 Sept 1964 to 13 Dec 1974, governor-general, Independence Act 1964; silent on the bases.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Malta' 1967..2024 (2 shapes, the same 474.7 km2 outline). Dossier start is 21 September 1964, so one new keyframe covers 1964-66. The seed lists kingdom-of-great-britain as a neighbour within 25 km in 1967-68, which the pages do not explain (Britain kept its bases until 31 March 1979 per the Malta page; this is another group's row). The 1979 gain is a caption-only event: land inside the outline passed from British control to the Maltese government and no cell changes colour. Pages silent: the Defence Agreement's signing year ('signed soon after' independence), Freedom Day beyond its date, Comino/Cominotto/Filfla, maritime boundaries, the list of governors-general and presidents (no rulers written), the date of UN and Commonwealth membership. 1980 neutrality, 2004 EU and 2008 euro dates are on the Malta page but are not territorial. No wars. Page budget 1-2 pages spent on 2.
